newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson optimistic for 1997 results.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson optimistic for 1997 results.

text.p: Giant retailer Dayton Hudson Corp Tuesday reported higher fiscal 1996 financial results and said it is optimistic about its 1997 performance.

"Entering fiscal 1996 our one priority was to improve the financial performance of Dayton Hudson and our results reflect our successful efforts to achieve higher returns," said Bob Ulrich, Dayton Hudson chairman and chief executive officer.
"We are optimistic about our performance in 1997 and look forward to continued improvement in our financial results," he said in a statement.

Dayton Hudson reported earnings before charges for its fiscal 1996 year ended February 1, 1997 increased 78 percent to $555 million from $311 million in fiscal 1995. Per share earnings rose 81 percent to $2.35 a share from $1.30 in 1995.
Fiscal 1996 net excludes a pre-tax charge of $134 million or $0.35 a share from repositioning of its real estate and after-tax charge of $11 million or $0.05 from debt redemption.
For the full year, total revenues rose eight percent to $25.37 billion, compared with $23.52 billion in 1995. Comparable-store revenues increased three percent for the fiscal year.

At year-end, Dayton Hudson said it had substantially reduced its retail debt as a percent of total capital to 50 percent, the middle of the company's target range. Due to strong earnings and enhanced merchandising management, the company said it was able to reduce its debt during the year while funding $1.3 billion in capital expenditures.
In 1996 net interest expense was equal to last year. The full-year tax rate was 39.5 percent, compared with 38.0 percent in the prior year.

Dayton Hudson operates large-store general merchandise formats, including discount stores, moderate-priced promotional and traditional department stores. The company currently operates 1,100 stores in 38 states. This includes 735 Target stores, 300 Mervyn's stores and 65 Department Stores.
